title: Annotatio III §.IV close: True image = Eucharistic bread as type; substance commanded vs human-effigy idolatry; stop before §.V
pass_a_gloss: And with a few things inserted: Let them exult and rejoice and enjoy freedom of tongue, whoever with sincerest mind desire and venerate and bring to the salvation of soul and body the true image of Christ, which our Lord God Himself, the high priest, taking an entire mass from us, around the time of the passion handed to His priests and initiates as a type and most efficacious remembrance: for when He was casting Himself spontaneously to death — that glorious and life-giving [death] — taking bread He blessed, after He had given thanks, and broke and giving to the disciples said: take, eat: This is My body. Behold therefore the image of that life-giving body which was honorably and gloriously exhibited. Because just as that which He assumed from us is matter alone, human substance, not perfectly expressed according to all things by which the person exists through itself, lest addition happen in the Divinity; so also He commanded the whole chosen image to be set forth — namely the substance of bread — lest idolatry be induced by a human effigy figured. Likewise also He willed the bread of the Eucharist, as a true image of natural flesh sanctified by the approach of the Holy Spirit, to be a divine body, and so it pleased Him &c. Read Sagittarius himself, pp. 354–355 and following.
pass_b_english: The true image of Christ they honor is what the High Priest Himself handed at the passion as type and efficacious remembrance: blessed, broken bread — ‘This is My body’.

As the assumed humanity is material substance (lest Divinity get an addition), so He commanded bread’s substance as the whole chosen image — lest a human effigy breed idolatry; Eucharist bread, Spirit-sanctified true image of natural flesh, He willed a divine body (Sagittarius pp. 354–355).
source_text: Et paucis intersertis: Exultent & lætentur & libertate linguæ fruantur, quicunque veram Christi imaginem sincerissimâ mente facientes desiderant & venerantur & ad salutem animæ corporisque adferunt, quam ipse Dominus noster Deus summus sacerdos, ex nobis integrè massam assumens, circa passionis tempus, in typum & recordationem efficacissimam, suis sacerdotibus & mystis tradidit: nam cum se sponte morti objiceret, gloriosa inquam illi & vivificanti, sumens panem benedixit, postquam gratias egisset & fregit tradensque discipulis dixit: accipite, manducate: Hoc est corpus meum. Ecce igitur vivificantis corporis illius imaginem quæ honorificè & gloriosè exhibita est. Quia quemadmodum id quòd è nobis assumsit, materia sola est substantia humana, juxta omnia non perfectè expressa, quæ per se existit persona, ne adjectio in Divinitate accidat; ita & imaginem totam electam, videlicet panis substantiam, mandavit apponi, ne scil. humanâ effigie figurata induceretur idololatria. Similiter etiam panem Eucharistæ veluti imaginem veram naturalis carnis per Sancti Spiritus aggressionem sanctificatam, divinum corpus esse voluit, illique sic placuit &c. &c. Lege ipsum Sagittarium p. m. 354. 355. & seq.
notes: True image = bread type; stop before §.V.
